title: Shuffle normalization of simplicial commutative algebras
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative ring and $P_ ullet$ a simplicial commutative $D$-algebra, with faces $d_i$ and degeneracies $s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Write $C(P)^{-n}=P_n$ for $n\geq0$, with differential $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$, zero differential out of degree zero, and zero positive terms. Put $J_n=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\operatorname{im}s_i$ as a $D$-submodule of $P_n$, with $J_0=0$. The quotient complex $N(P)^{-n}=P_n/J_n$ has multiplication
$$[x]\mathbin{\mathrm{sh}}[y]=\sum_{(\mu,
u)}\operatorname{sgn}(\mu,
u)[(s_{
u_q}\cdots s_{
u_1}x)(s_{\mu_p}\cdots s_{\mu_1}y)],\qquad x\in P_p,\ y\in P_q,$$
where $\mu_1<\cdots<\mu_p$ and $
u_1<\cdots<
u_q$ partition $\{0,\ldots,p+q-1\}$ and the sign is that of the permutation listed as $(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_p,
u_1,\ldots,
u_q)$. Empty degeneracy strings are identities. These formulas are well-defined and make $N(P)$ an associative unital graded-commutative dg $D$-algebra [def-sfb-dg-derived-category], with unit $[1]\in P_0/J_0$ and $d(xy)=d(x)y+(-1)^p x\,d(y)$ for $|x|=-p$. This construction is functorial in simplicial $D$-algebra maps.

The quotient $C(P)	o N(P)$ is a natural quasi-isomorphism, and each $P_n/J_n$ is a direct summand of the $D$-module $P_n$. Consequently, if every $P_n$ is flat over $D$, so is every term of $N(P)$. If $P_ ullet	o E$ is an augmentation to a constant commutative $D$-algebra and $C(P)	o E[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, its induced augmentation $N(P)	o E[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of dg $D$-algebras. For a constant simplicial algebra $D$, $N(D)$ is canonically $D[0]$.

source.place: Tags 017V (lemma-splitting-abelian-category), 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), 019C (lemma-quasi-isomorphism), for additive normalization and its quotient model. The displayed shuffle multiplication and its dg algebra laws are an agent-stated additional prerequisite, not asserted by those tags; WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Section 8.5 (Eilenberg-Zilber).

proof.text: Work first with homological degree $n$, reindexed as cohomological degree $-n$ at the end. Functoriality in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] gives the face and degeneracy identities by composing the corresponding monotone maps. In the double alternating sum for $\partial^2$, the two deletions of positions $i<j$ have coefficients $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$, so cancel. For $s_i z\in J_n$, the terms $d_i s_i z=d_{i+1}s_i z=z$ cancel in $\partial s_i z$; the terms with $k<i$ are $s_{i-1}d_k z$ and those with $k>i+1$ are $s_i d_{k-1}z$. All lie in $J_{n-1}$. For $n=1$ only the cancelling terms remain. Thus $J$ is a subcomplex and $q:C(P)\to C(P)/J$ is a chain map. Maps of simplicial algebras preserve $J$ and commute with $q$.

source.place: Tags 017V (lemma-splitting-abelian-category), 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), remark-degenerate-subcomplex and 019C (lemma-quasi-isomorphism). Positive-face convention checked directly below.

proof.text: Put $K_0=P_0$ and $K_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker d_i$. On $P_n$ write $E_j=1-s_{j-1}d_j$, $1\leq j\leq n$, and $\rho_n=E_1E_2\cdots E_n$ (rightmost applied first), with $\rho_0=1$. If $d_k z=0$ for $k>j$, then $d_jE_jz=0$, since $d_js_{j-1}=1$, and for $k>j$ one has $d_kE_jz=d_kz-s_{j-1}d_{k-1}d_jz=d_kz-s_{j-1}d_jd_kz=0$. Descending induction on $j$ therefore gives $\rho_n(P_n)\subset K_n$. Each $E_j$ fixes $K_n$ and changes an element by a degeneracy, so $\rho_n|_{K_n}=1$ and $z-\rho_nz\in J_n$. These conclusions include $n=0$.

source.place: Tags 017V (lemma-splitting-abelian-category), 019A (lemma-decompose-associated-complexes), remark-degenerate-subcomplex and 019C (lemma-quasi-isomorphism). Positive-face convention checked directly below.

proof.text: For $0\leq i<n$ and $j>i+1$, the simplicial identities give $E_j^{(n)}s_i=s_i E_{j-1}^{(n-1)}$: expand both sides and use $d_js_i=s_i d_{j-1}$ and $s_{j-1}s_i=s_i s_{j-2}$. Commute $s_i$ left across $E_n,E_{n-1},\ldots,E_{i+2}$ in $\rho_ns_i$. The next factor is $E_{i+1}s_i=s_i-s_i d_{i+1}s_i=0$. Thus $\rho_nJ_n=0$. Together with the preceding step, this proves $P_n=K_n\oplus J_n$: every $z$ is $\rho_nz+(z-\rho_nz)$, and an element in the intersection is both fixed and killed by $\rho_n$. In particular $a_n=q_n|_{K_n}:K_n\to P_n/J_n$ is an isomorphism with inverse $[z]\mapsto\rho_nz$.

proof.text: For $z\in K_n$, the alternating differential is $d_0z$, and $d_i d_0z=d_0d_{i+1}z=0$ for $1\leq i<n$. Thus $K$ is the positive-face Moore complex, and its inclusion $i:K\to C(P)$ is a chain map. Hence $a=qi$ is a chain map and, by the degreewise inverses just constructed, an isomorphism of complexes $K\cong N(P)$. In particular $q$ is a split surjection in each degree with section $i_na_n^{-1}$, satisfying $q_ni_na_n^{-1}=1$ and $i_na_n^{-1}q_n=\rho_n$. Every operator defining $\rho$ commutes with simplicial module maps, so these splittings and the quotient maps are natural.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence] in the abelian category of $D$-modules, to the underlying simplicial module of $P$. Its $N(X)$ is exactly $K$ (kernels of the positive faces, differential $d_0$), so the map $i$ above is a chain homotopy equivalence. Reindex degree $n$ as $-n$ and extend by zero; its inverse and homotopies retain their equations. By [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology], the induced maps of $i$ and its homotopy inverse are mutually inverse on cohomology. Since $a=qi$ is an isomorphism, $H(q)=H(a)H(i)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism in every degree. This proves the asserted natural quasi-isomorphism $C(P)\to N(P)$.

proof.text:
For a shuffle partition $(\mu,
u)$ of $\{0,\ldots,p+q-1\}$, set $A_k=\#(\mu\cap[0,k))$, $B_k=\#(
u\cap[0,k))$. These define monotone surjections $A:[p+q]	o[p]$, $B:[p+q]	o[q]$. The repeats of $A$ are precisely $
u$, so $P(A)x=s_{
u_q}\cdots s_{
u_1}x$; likewise $P(B)y=s_{\mu_p}\cdots s_{\mu_1}y$. Define $b(x,y)=\sum\operatorname{sgn}(\mu,
u)P(A)x\,P(B)y$ in $P_{p+q}$. Every operator is $D$-linear and multiplication in each $P_n$ is $D$-bilinear, so $b$ is bilinear. This is exactly the representative formula in the statement, including empty blocks.

proof.text: To check its differential, apply [lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary] with parameter simplices $[p],[q]$, and the identity strings $u=(0,\ldots,p)$, $v=(0,\ldots,q)$. For each $m$, evaluate a basis string of $V(p,q)_m$, equivalently monotone maps $\alpha:[m]\to[p]$, $\beta:[m]\to[q]$, at $P(\alpha)x\,P(\beta)y\in P_m$, and extend $\mathbf Z$-linearly. Deleting vertex $k$ before evaluation is the same as applying $d_k$ afterwards, because $d_k$ is a ring map. The evaluated shuffle is $b(x,y)$. An input face deleting $i$ evaluates to $d_ix$ or $d_iy$, since $P(\delta_i\alpha)=P(\alpha)d_i$. The cited boundary identity therefore gives $\partial b(x,y)=b(\partial x,y)+(-1)^p b(x,\partial y)$, omitting a term when its input degree is zero. This argument uses integral coefficients, so imposes no restriction on $D$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inherited coefficient-model prerequisite. Agent-written shuffle calculation; the blueprint gives the application only. WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, section 8.5.

proof.text: If $x=s_i z$, each shuffle summand is degenerate separately. Indeed let $k$ be the edge of its lattice path on which $A$ increases from $i$ to $i+1$. The maps $\sigma_iA$ and $B$ both repeat at the adjacent vertices $k,k+1$. Write them as $\alpha'\sigma_k$ and $\beta'\sigma_k$. The summand is then $s_k(P(\alpha')z)\,s_k(P(\beta')y)=s_k(P(\alpha')z\,P(\beta')y)$, in $J_{p+q}$. If $y=s_i z$, use the edge on which $B$ crosses $i$ instead. Bilinearity now gives $b(J_p,P_q)+b(P_p,J_q)\subset J_{p+q}$. Thus $b$ descends to the displayed product on $N(P)$, and the preceding boundary formula descends to its Leibniz rule. No claim that $J_n$ is an ideal for the ordinary product on $P_n$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inherited coefficient-model prerequisite. Agent-written shuffle calculation; the blueprint gives the application only. WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, section 8.5.

proof.text: For $x\in P_p,y\in P_q,z\in P_r$, expand $b(b(x,y),z)$. Its indices are an outer word in the letters $AB,C$ and an inner word in $A,B$. Replace, in order, the outer $AB$ letters by the inner letters. This bijects the indices with all words containing $p$ letters $A$, $q$ letters $B$, $r$ letters $C$; the inverse deletes all $C$ letters for the inner word and merges $A,B$ for the outer word. Expanding $b(x,b(y,z))$ gives the same words by deleting $A$ and merging $B,C$. In either expansion the three simplicial operators are the prefix counts of $A,B,C$, because composing prefix-count maps counts exactly those letters. Multiplicativity of simplicial operators and associativity in $P_{p+q+r}$ give identical terms. Both coefficient products equal $(-1)^I$, where $I$ counts inverted pairs for the order $A<B<C$: the inner and outer counts partition these pairs. Hence the expansions agree, also when any count is zero. The quotient product is associative.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inherited coefficient-model prerequisite. Agent-written shuffle calculation; the blueprint gives the application only. WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, section 8.5.

proof.text: Swapping the blocks of a $(p,q)$ shuffle bijects it with a $(q,p)$ shuffle. The signs differ by $(-1)^{pq}$, since the block interchange moves $p$ entries past $q$ entries. The two term factors interchange, and they commute in $P_{p+q}$. Therefore $b(y,x)=(-1)^{pq}b(x,y)$, giving the required graded commutativity since $(-p)(-q)$ has parity $pq$. For $(0,q)$ there is one shuffle, all degeneracies applied to $1\in P_0$ still equal $1$, and its product with $y$ is $y$; the $(p,0)$ case is identical. Thus $[1]$ is a two-sided unit, and its differential is zero. Elements of $D$ enter centrally by $D\to P_0$; the same one-shuffle computation agrees with scalar multiplication.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inherited coefficient-model prerequisite. Agent-written shuffle calculation; the blueprint gives the application only. WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, section 8.5.

proof.text: A simplicial $D$-algebra map $f:P\to P'$ commutes term by term with $P(A),P(B)$ and with multiplication, so $f(b(x,y))=b(fx,fy)$. It preserves the degree-zero unit and is already a map on the quotient complexes by step 1. Thus it induces a dg $D$-algebra map. The associative multiplication and closed unit from steps 9–10, together with the Leibniz identity of steps 7–8, give precisely the dg-algebra structure of [def-sfb-dg-derived-category] on the underlying integer cochain complex, now with its specified central $D$-action. The construction respects identities and composites because its underlying quotient maps do.

source.place: Paragraph (3), inherited coefficient-model prerequisite. Agent-written shuffle calculation; the blueprint gives the application only. WANTED Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, section 8.5.

proof.text: For each $n$, take $M=P_n$, $N=P_n/J_n$, $r=q_n$ and $i=i_na_n^{-1}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract]. The relation $ri=1$ was proved in steps 3–4 and both maps are $D$-linear. Consequently if $P_n$ is flat over $D$, so is $P_n/J_n$. The zero positive cochain terms are flat as well: tensoring with zero sends every injection to the injection $0\to0$.

proof.text: In a constant simplicial algebra $E$, every degeneracy is the identity, hence $J_n=E$ for $n>0$ and $J_0=0$. Thus $N(E)=E[0]$, with its ordinary product by the $(0,0)$ formula. Functoriality therefore sends an augmentation $P\to E$ to a dg-algebra map $N(P)\to E[0]$. The original chain augmentation $\epsilon:C(P)\to E[0]$ factors as $\bar\epsilon q$ (in positive degrees its target is zero, in degree zero $q_0=1$). If $\epsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism, then $H(\bar\epsilon)=H(\epsilon)H(q)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism in every degree, proving the final augmentation assertion. Taking $E=D$ also gives the stated canonical identification $N(D)=D[0]$.
